issues: No sign of getting around the measurement. The edit only changes how the RF and SVR predictions are combined: it averages z-scores instead of normalized ranks. The mean and sd come from each model's own predictions on the test set, never from test labels. This is a fixed rescaling within each fold, so it is legitimate for a Spearman-based score.
No bug that would make the result meaningless. The code returns one finite prediction per test molecule, and the 1e-9 term guards against dividing by zero.

My z is close to the harness value. Candidate minus incumbent is 0.4732 - 0.4718 = 0.0014. With one run each and noise sd 0.0070, the sd of the difference is 0.0070*sqrt(2) ≈ 0.0099, which gives z ≈ -0.14 (negative means the candidate is worse). The harness reports -0.137. The small gap is consistent with rounding of the displayed 4-decimal losses.
The difference is well inside the noise, so the decision to reject is reasonable. The change brings no measurable gain, and the incumbent's rank average is equally simple.
